reviews.summary: Jason calls the 15m Juice D/LAB his favorite light-wind kite. Against the Sonic 5 it was far lighter on the bar, quicker to turn, floated and relaunched easily, and stayed flyable in 10–12 knots, so it is much easier to use. The foil kite won clearly on lift, hangtime and upwind once he had learned it.

structured_review.summary: Jason Montreal's go-to light-wind kite: very light on the bar, responsive and easy to keep flying and relaunch in as little as 10–12 knots. It is far simpler to live with than a foil kite, but a Sonic 5 jumps clearly higher with more hangtime and goes upwind better once its timing is learned.
pros: Very light bar and steering pressure for a 15m
Quick, responsive steering; feels a size smaller than a 15m foil kite
Floats and relaunches easily, even in very light wind
Flyable in 10–12 knots with essentially no learning curve
cons: Clearly less lift and hangtime than a foil kite like the Sonic 5
Gets less upwind and less consistent jump height than a foil in 13–18 knots
structured_review.best_for: Riders wanting a hassle-free light-wind LEI that relaunches easily and needs no foil-kite skills.
structured_review.not_for: Light-wind riders chasing maximum boost and hangtime who are ready to learn a foil kite.
structured_review.rec_blurb: The easy way to ride light wind: featherweight bar and easy relaunch.
